arrival.note: A BOUND FROM THE RECORD, NOT AN ARRIVAL. poll_1833 names this person at Chicago by 31 December 1833 and nothing says when they came. The bound is at or before the scene date, so the person was at Chicago by 1 July 1835 on this record's own evidence.

arrival_year.note: DRAWN, NOT READ. The household's arrival block holds a BOUND — somebody was here by 1833-12-31 and no source says when they came — so the year is drawn from the arrival years the known layer records, truncated at that bound and renormalised. It says what a household of this bound most likely was, and nothing whatever about this household.

occupation.note: No source in this pass's evidence records an occupation for this person. A poll list, a tax list, a muster roll and a baptismal entry each print a name and no trade, and where a later directory prints one it is a trade of 1843 — T-0633 is the rule for back-projecting that, and this pass does not have it.

dated_bounds.list_title: Poll list of the first election of the Board of Trustees of the Town of Chicago, 10 August 1833
dated_bounds.identity_discriminator: forenames agree initial for initial: entry 'James Gilbert' against resident 'James Gilbert'
dated_bounds.identity_rule: one resident of the surname 'Gilbert' agrees with the entry's forenames; 1 bearer(s) of the surname were considered.
dated_bounds.note: A BOUND ON PRESENCE, AND NOTHING FURTHER. Poll list of the first election of the Board of Trustees of the Town of Chicago, 10 August 1833 records a man who presented himself and voted, so the entry places a body in Chicago no later than 1833-08-10. Under the evidence ladder ratified 2026-09-03 a source EARLIER than the scene date corroborates and dates and never promotes: a man on a roll of 1833, 1834 or 1835 is not thereby at Chicago on 1 July 1835. THE IDENTITY IS INFERRED AND THE PAGE IS NOT. The reading of the roll is documented — the town's own paper, held by the Illinois Regional Archives Depository, twice mediated by Schulz's transcription and Genealogy Trails' republication, which this project has not gone behind. What no source states is that the man on the roll is the person on this card: data/research/civic/voter_crosswalk.json joins them on a name, by its rule “one resident of the surname 'Gilbert' agrees with the entry's forenames; 1 bearer(s) of the surname were considered.”, and forenames agree initial for initial: entry 'James Gilbert' against resident 'James Gilbert'. A bound whose subject is inferred is an inferred bound. No grade moves here and the identity is neither reopened nor hardened.

persons.note: THE LADDER'S OWN READING OF THIS EVIDENCE. Read from newspaper_letter_list, poll_1833. THE GRADE IS THE OWNER'S RATIFIED LADDER OF 2026-09-03 (G1c), applied to every identity at once by tools/consolidate_resident_evidence.py and spent onto this card by tools/mint_civic_residents.py; the evidence blocks below carry the reading AS READ, its locator and the record it came from, so the page can be gone back to. WHAT IS RECONSTRUCTED: everything except the person and the sources — no dwelling, no trade, no origin, no family, no party. A BOUND FROM THE RECORD, NOT AN ARRIVAL. poll_1833 names this person at Chicago by 31 December 1833 and nothing says when they came. The bound is at or before the scene date, so the person was at Chicago by 1 July 1835 on this record's own evidence. No figure is drawn (L1). THE TOWN'S OWN ROLLS, 1833-1835 — CORROBORATION, NOT A GRADE. The early Chicago voter and tax lists held by the Illinois Regional Archives Depository name this person 1 time: Poll list of the first election of the Board of Trustees of the Town of Chicago, 10 August 1833 — “Gilbert, James” (poll_1833_012, line 33). These are the town's own contemporary paper rather than a recollection of it, and each appearance says that a man of that name stood on that roll in that year — no more. The reading is twice mediated (Schulz's transcription, then Genealogy Trails' republication) and this project has not seen the IRAD originals. Under the ratified ladder (T-0513) the 1835 poll with a second independent source is attested, the 1835 poll alone or a 1833/1834 list with another source is inferred, and a single appearance with nothing else is a projected resident. This pass WRITES THE EVIDENCE AND MOVES NO GRADE — T-0515 applies the ladder against every source at once. Identity by the crosswalk's own rule: one resident of the surname 'Gilbert' agrees with the entry's forenames; 1 bearer(s) of the surname were considered. (data/research/civic/voter_crosswalk.json).

basis.note: Drawn from the 1840 Chicago schedule's column 'free white males 40 under 50', one of its male bands, conditioned on `civic_list_20_and_over` because the person stands on a poll, a tax list or a muster roll.

replaceable_by.match: a source that states this person's age, their birth year, or an interval either can be read out of

age_band.note: AN AGE BAND, NEVER A YEAR. No source this project holds bears on when this person was born, so the band is drawn from the only committed sex by age distribution the project has - the 1840 Chicago schedule, five years after the scene and a town twice the size - seeded by this person's own id ('gilbert_james:age_bands_1840'). AND THE CONDITIONING IS THE MODEL'S, NOT A SOURCE'S: that a poll, tax or muster list names a person 20 or over - the 1840 schedule's own adult line. THE FRANCHISE'S AGE RULE IS NOT IN ANY SOURCE RECORD THIS PROJECT HOLDS; this is the model's conditioning and not a reading (T-1303's finding, handed to T-1304). No exact year is written, because a year drawn from a decadal band would read as a record of a birth.

sex_basis.note: A FORENAME THAT STANDS IN ONE SEX'S NAMING ONLY. 'James' is read as male because 2 persons in this layer whose sex a source records bear it (couch_james, kinzie_james), and it stands in the irish and yankee male forename pool of this town's own attested naming. Nothing about this person is recorded; the name is the whole of the reasoning, and the table that licenses it — data/research/residents/forename_sex.json — refuses a name its own evidence splits, refuses Jean, Marion, Leslie and Francis by name, and refuses an initial outright.
